extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners/representatives, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on requesting, authorizing, scheduling, and conducting interviews between patent applicants (and their representatives) and USPTO examiners, including in-person, telephone, and MS Teams video conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are an opportunity to explain rejections, discuss prior art, clarify positions, and resolve issues. They lead to a better understanding of the invention and grounds of rejection, bridge the understanding gap between the examiner and the applicant, are an effective method for reaching agreement and advancing prosecution, and help to promote compact prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews to explain reasoning and to seek agreement or resolution; they should be used to improve mutual understanding and move prosecution forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and constraints for in-person interviews (COVID-19 update)
rubrics_metrics.description: In-person interviews are available and may be requested, however the teleworking option and the location of the examiner may limit availability. Examiners with a reporting requirement to a USPTO campus may conduct an in-person interview if requested. Public interview rooms in all locations are currently closed while equipment is updated to work with MS Teams. Visitors are held to the same COVID-19 policies as employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request in-person interviews but expect limits due to telework and facility status; consider video conference alternatives when in-person isn't practicable. Check USPTO coronavirus updates for current policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet authorization required for email responses (MPEP 502.03(II))
rubrics_metrics.description: Without Internet authorization by the applicant in place, the examiner cannot respond via email to any Internet correspondence which contains information subject to the confidentiality requirement as set forth in 35 U.S.C. 122.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain authorization before expecting email communications from the examiner; authorization can be written or a one-time oral authorization (limited scope). See MPEP citation for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written authorization to communicate electronically (preferred method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written authorization, when properly submitted, allows the examiner and applicant to communicate electronically for the entirety of the application process, or until the applicant withdraws the authorization. The preferred way to submit written authorization is by using the PTO/SB/439 form (Authorization for Internet communications...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable submission methods include Patent Electronic Systems (EFS-Web or Patent Center), U.S. Postal Service, USPTO customer service window, or central fax. Written authorization persists until withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable language and record for written authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may create their own authorization document using provided language: "Recognizing that internet communications are not secure, I hereby authorize the USPTO to communicate... by video conferencing, instant messaging, or electronic mail. I understand that a copy of these communications will be made of record in the application file."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not using PTO/SB/439, include clear language authorizing electronic communications and acknowledging recordation; follow acceptable submission channels listed for written authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time oral authorization for video conference interviews (MPEP 713.01(II))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant or applicant’s representative may verbally request and authorize a video conference interview instead of submitting a written request. This one-time oral authorization is intended to make scheduling more efficient but must be noted on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-time oral authorization is limited to the scheduling and conducting of the specific video conference interview being arranged and does not extend to other internet or email communications regarding the application. Make sure the oral authorization details are recorded in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the AIR form to request interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Automated Interview Request (AIR) form is an online tool that permits applicants to schedule an interview, giving 24-hour access from anywhere to request an interview. The examiner will respond to the AIR request within 2 business days, using either phone or email. The AIR form includes options for submitting internet authorization if not previously submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the AIR form (https://www.uspto.gov/interviewpractice) to efficiently request interviews and to provide or confirm internet authorization. Expect examiner response within two business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview agendas — usefulness and non-requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agendas are extremely useful in helping examiners prepare for an upcoming interview and can lead to a more productive interview. An agenda need not be an exhaustive list of intended matters for discussion. An interview without an agenda can still be held with adequate preparation, and lack of an agenda alone is not grounds for an interview to be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an agenda to improve productivity and examiner preparation, but do not assume an agenda is mandatory. Keep agendas focused on key issues to be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Action Interview (FAI) pilot program status and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAI pilot started in May 2011 and has been discontinued; the last day to file a request to participate was January 15, 2021. Historically the program had over 16,000 participating applications; some applications remain in process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request participation in the discontinued FAI pilot; be aware of historical context and remaining applications from the pilot that may still be in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video conference policy: MS Teams and link origin
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO has switched to using Microsoft (MS) Teams for all video conference interviews with examiners. Authorization for electronic communication is required either in writing or orally. The link to the MS Teams meeting must come from the examiner; examiners are not permitted to conduct video conference interviews using links generated by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect MS Teams as the platform; do not send or rely on applicant-generated meeting links. Ensure appropriate authorization is recorded prior to electronic meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS Teams sharing and presenter designation
rubrics_metrics.description: To share content in MS Teams, use the Share button and select the type of content to share. Click 'Window' to present a specific open program. If you do not have the option to share, inform the examiner and they can designate you as a presenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the content you intend to share (specific windows or apps). If sharing a whiteboard, select 'Microsoft Whiteboard' via Share to collaborate. Coordinate presenter role with the examiner if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview resources for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview specialists are subject matter experts in each technology center on interview practice and policy and are available to assist applicants and examiners. A listing of interview specialists and contact resources (including the Interview Practice Mailbox ExaminerInterviewPractice@USPTO.GOV) and links to Microsoft Teams help are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reach out to interview specialists or the Interview Practice Mailbox with questions about interviews; consult provided Microsoft Teams resources for technical guidance.
